html:
SMTO-UI-0057 — Sign in to continue

GUID: d9151aa1-7b11-5d75-8388-272e1f3e97a7
Slug: authentication-required
Domain: UI · Subsystem: authentication

What happened

  • Your browser isn't signed in to SMTO any more, so the server didn't accept this request. Sign-ins end after 12 hours, when you sign out, or when your password is changed or reset.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Copy any text you typed but haven't sent yet, so you can paste it back later. SMTO sends you to the sign-in page, which reloads the page and can clear unsent text.
  2. On the Sign in to your workspace page, enter your username and password and select Sign in. Your earlier sign-in ended, and SMTO only accepts requests from a signed-in browser.
  3. Open the task or item you were working on and check whether your last change is already there before doing it again. This request was refused, but something you started just before your sign-in ended may still have finished.

What success looks like

  • Your account and workspace load, and your latest work appears.

If it still fails

  • If SMTO sends you straight back to the sign-in page after you sign in, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Never include your password or browser cookies.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Sign in to continue.

What this means

  • Your browser does not have a valid session for this request. This reports access to the current request, not the outcome of previous operations.

Why this can happen

  • Your browser does not have a valid session for this request.

How to diagnose it

  • Your account and current workspace load.

How to fix it

  • The portal middleware returned authentication_required (401) because no valid session cookie came with an API request (session expired after 12 hours, signed out, or revoked by a password change, an administrator password reset, or a change to the account's role, username or enabled status); WebSockets are closed with code 1008 instead. Sign in again, then reload the latest task or saved item before repeating any write: the rejected request did not run, but earlier requests may have.
  • Sign in again, then inspect the latest task or saved change before repeating an earlier action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Your account and current workspace load.

How to verify the fix

  • Your account and current workspace load.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Authentication guidance never changes account permissions or replays task work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
